prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
The blog is up and running at **https://localhost:44317/**. The front page lists both posts, and all three pages return 200 with every block rendering (none fall back to "Could not render component"). I created all content types, media and content through the MCP server, with no migrations, and uSync exported the changes to `uSync/v18/`. I didn't open the site in a browser, so I've only checked the HTML and image URLs, not how it looks.

**How to view it**
- Front page: https://localhost:44317/ — it has the domain `/`, so it answers at the root.
- Post 1: https://localhost:44317/mcp-is-the-usb-c-port-for-ai/
- Post 2: https://localhost:44317/this-blog-was-built-through-mcp/
- Backoffice: https://localhost:44317/umbraco (admin@example.com / 1234567890)

Umbraco is still running in the background from my session.

**What I built**
- **Blocks** (in the Blocks folder): `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`. The post list shows the blog's posts newest first, with an optional maximum.
- **Block grids:** two 12-column grids, *Blog Front Page Grid* and *Blog Post Grid*. They were filed under `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid` automatically.
- **Pages** (in the Pages folder):
  - `blogFrontPage` sits under WWW and only allows posts as children. I updated the site root type to allow it.
  - `blogPost` has the block grid plus *Publish Date*, *Excerpt* and *Teaser Image* on a Listing tab, which the front-page list uses.
  - Each page type has its own template, both sharing a `layout` template.
- **Media:** six Unsplash photos imported into a *Blog* media folder, each credited to its photographer.
- **Content:** the *Blog* front page (hero plus post list) and two posts, built from hero, rich text, quote and image blocks:
  - "MCP Is the USB-C Port for AI" — includes a half-width image next to half-width text.
  - "This Blog Was Built Through MCP"
- **Razor:** done after a stop, build and restart, following the block pipeline in AGENTS.md:
  - One adapter per block in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml`.
  - Plain view models in `Models/Blocks/`.
  - One ViewComponent per block in `ViewComponents/`.
  - All markup in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
  - Pages render their blocks with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`.
- **Styling:** Tailwind. I added CSS for the block grid layout and rich text to `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css` and ran the frontend build.

**Problems and things to know**
- **Focal points from the MCP import:** `create-media-multiple` gave every image a focal point of `{left: 0, top: 0.5}`, so every crop was pinned to the left edge. I re-centered all six through MCP with `update-media`. Watch for this on future imports.
- **Node in Git Bash:** the shell profile doesn't set up `fnm`, so `npm` only worked from PowerShell. Rebuild the CSS there with `fnm env --shell powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`, then `npm run build` in the Frontend folder.
- **Small changes to existing files:**
  - I added the project's model and block-model namespaces to `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml`.
  - I put the ViewComponent classes in a new `ViewComponents/` folder, since AGENTS.md doesn't say where they belong.
- **Not built:**
  - No block settings (spacing, background, anchor) and no block grid areas.
  - The *Publish Date* shown on posts is a manual field, separate from Umbraco's own publish date.
